name: Renaissance (Rinascimento)
description: Renaissance (Rinascimento) — the rich humanist palette of Italian masters, from lapis lazuli ultramarine to Tuscan earth and gold leaf

foundation.story: The Italian Renaissance (14th–17th century) transformed art through oil painting, linear perspective, and a palette derived from mineral pigments traded across the Mediterranean. Ultramarine from Afghan lapis lazuli cost more than gold. Tuscan earth pigments — sienna, umber, ochre — grounded compositions in warmth. Gold leaf connected human achievement to divine light. The palette of Raphael, Titian, and Botticelli remains the Western canon's richest.
foundation.philosophy: Rinascimento — the rebirth of classical learning, humanist confidence in beauty and proportion

seedColors.name: Oltremare (Ultramarine)
seedColors.tradition: From lapis lazuli mined in Badakhshan, Afghanistan — ground, purified, and mixed with oil. More expensive than gold per ounce, it was reserved for the Virgin Mary's robe.
seedColors.source: Color: A Natural History of the Palette, Victoria Finlay

seedColors.name: Terra di Siena (Sienna Earth)
seedColors.tradition: Burnt sienna — iron-rich earth from Tuscany, heated to deepen its red-brown warmth. The shadow tone in chiaroscuro painting from Leonardo to Caravaggio.
seedColors.source: The Materials and Techniques of Medieval Painting, Daniel V. Thompson

seedColors.name: Oro (Gold Leaf)
seedColors.tradition: Beaten gold applied to gesso grounds in tempera painting. From Giotto's haloes to Ghiberti's bronze doors, gold represented divine light breaking through the earthly plane.
seedColors.source: The Craftsman's Handbook (Il Libro dell'Arte), Cennino Cennini

seedColors.name: Verdaccio
seedColors.tradition: A green-grey earth underpainting used to model flesh tones before color layers. The structural skeleton of Renaissance portraiture.

seedColors.name: Pergamena (Parchment)
seedColors.tradition: Calfskin vellum — the surface for illuminated manuscripts from Petrarch's sonnets to Leonardo's notebooks. Warm, organic, never pure white.
seedColors.source: The Art of Renaissance Europe, Boskovits & Brown

seedColors.name: Ombra Naturale (Raw Umber)
seedColors.tradition: Manganese-rich earth from Umbria — the deep brown of shadow and depth. Essential for the sfumato technique of Leonardo da Vinci.
seedColors.source: The Materials and Techniques of Medieval Painting, Daniel V. Thompson
